# Rabbit Brain

> The research state for ML work done with coding agents: claims with criteria fixed in advance, settings with where each value came from, evidence with a receipt, kept as plain files in `.rb/` next to the code. Agents propose; `rb` checks the sources and computes the verdicts; people decide. Release review for iterative perception models (optical flow, stereo, depth) is built in as `rb review`, and its runs attach as evidence. `pip install rabbit-brain`, then `rb docs`.

If a project has a `.rb/` directory, an agent runs `rb context` before anything else: it is the state of the work, and it replaces any summary of it. The agent adds questions, hypotheses, experiments with their variants, settings with their sources, claims and evidence; `rb` verifies a setting only by reading its source and finding the value stated there, and computes every claim's verdict from its evidence each time it is read. It must not compute verdicts, regressions or rankings itself.

What an agent must pass on to the person, because a summary that drops it is misleading: a claim's standing exactly as `rb show` prints it (`supported, not established` is not `supported`), every blocking reason, and which settings are provisional rather than verified. Freezing an experiment, deciding, amending a frozen spec and retracting what something rests on are the person's calls; `rb` refuses them from an agent and returns the exact command to hand over (`errors[0].handoff.command`).

For a release review: a case the report marks **borderline** turns on a margin thinner than the difference between two machines; the stability limits are generic heuristics; if the receipt says the adapter did not agree with the model repository's own evaluation, that comes first.

## Docs

- [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rabbit-brain/rb/main/AGENTS.md): the complete manual for agents and humans: the rules, the research-state commands, sources and what "verified" means, when a claim is established, release review, the JSON output, exit codes, every error code with its fix, what to report to the person.
- [README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rabbit-brain/rb/main/README.md): what it does, what it does not do, one real evidence sheet.
- [CHANGELOG.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rabbit-brain/rb/main/CHANGELOG.md): what each version added.

## Package

- [PyPI: rabbit-brain](https://pypi.org/project/rabbit-brain/): `pip install rabbit-brain` (core, pydantic only), `[yaml]` to read YAML configs, `[raft]` for the RAFT review adapter, `[evidence]` for evidence sheets with a custom adapter. Python 3.10 or later. CLI: `rb`. `rb` uploads nothing unless you run `rb workspace push`.
- [Source](https://github.com/rabbit-brain/rb): Apache-2.0.

## Examples

- [examples/raft-kitti](https://github.com/rabbit-brain/rb/tree/main/examples/raft-kitti): four real reviews of the official RAFT checkpoints on KITTI-2015 with their receipts, findings and evidence sheets.

## Optional

- `rb review init --demo` writes a synthetic project so the review workflow runs on any machine in seconds; every output of it says it is synthetic, and evidence from it never counts toward a claim.
